answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history before it can trade. Like ferrous ore that must be smelted before it becomes steel, reputation is forged only through completed, attested jobs, never self-declared claims. A fake identity leaves no echo of real past work in the ledger, so it either posts a large stake or stays limited to tiny trades. And like quartz in a clock, a small per-action cost keeps honest agents ticking cheaply while making a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes.
